newsitem.title: INDIA: Mercedes-Benz India to hike E-Class prices.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes-Benz India to hike E-Class prices.

text.p: Mercedes Benz India Ltd on Thursday announced a hike ranging from four percent to six percent in the prices of its 'E' class cars.
"This marginal price increase is the first price adjustment undertaken by MBIL since the car was launched in October 1995," the firm said in a statement.
The price of the 'E' class diesel version (E220) will rise six percent from mid-July, the firm said, and that of the petrol version (E250D) by four percent.

A series of bulk export orders coupled with an increase in domestic demand recently prompted Mercedes-Benz to double production at its plant at the western city of Pune near Bombay, the statement added.
"Since March 1997, Mercedes-Benz has already exported 500 E-class cars to Asia, Africa and southern Europe," the statement said.
Mercedes-Benz said it planned to produce around 3,000 units in 1998 for domestic and export markets, with the production volume increasing over the following years to 5,000 units.
